sources.entry: flit-core - Minimal, dependency-free build backend for pure-Python packages.

summary.one_liner: Flit is a simple tool for publishing pure-Python packages and single-file modules to PyPI with minimal packaging configuration.
summary.what_it_does: Flit lets you package a Python module or package by running "flit init" to generate a pyproject.toml, then "flit publish" to upload it to PyPI. It takes the import name as the PyPI name and automatically includes all subpackages and data files within a package. The README says it reads the module's docstring summary and __version__ to fill in metadata. It provides "flit install" for local development, with an optional --symlink flag and a --python flag to pick an interpreter. Older flit.ini files can be converted to pyproject.toml with "python3 -m flit.tomlify". The README also names flit-core as a build backend, which is what pip uses when installing an sdist.
use_cases: publish a pure-Python package to PyPI
build a wheel or sdist for a Python project
install a package in editable/development mode
generate pyproject.toml for a simple Python module
notable: Minimal configuration: infers metadata from the module docstring and __version__
Packages a single importable module or package, using the import name as the PyPI name
Includes subpackages and data files automatically
Provides flit-core as a build backend for pyproject.toml-based builds
Can convert legacy flit.ini files to pyproject.toml
caveats: Requires Python 3 to run; Python 2 modules can be distributed only if importable on Python 3
Packages one importable module or package at a time
